text:
The Avalanche lost Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar within minutes of each other in Ottawa on Thursday, both with lower-body injuries, and the whole night in Montreal turns on whether either can play. Coach Jared Bednar had no update after the game, and USA Today listed both as questionable. MacKinnon leads Colorado with 30 points; Makar has 23. What happened after they left was almost as interesting: the Avalanche came back from 2-0 down to lead in the third before losing 4-3 in overtime. Our numbers still price MacKinnon (81% for a point) as if he plays; if he doesn't, Colorado's chances look different than its 3.27 expected goals tonight suggest.

Montreal is the hottest team in the building. The Canadiens have points in twelve straight (9-0-3), and Cole Caufield made history against Boston on Thursday, becoming the first player since Auston Matthews with a 12-goals-in-12-games stretch against the Bruins (98.5 The Sports Hub). The caution is in how they're winning: 50% of the expected goals during the run, with Jacob Fowler doing a lot of lifting at .926 and 13.5 goals saved above expected. Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and the speculation about how long has been loud in Montreal.

Colorado's depth is the question either way. Gabriel Landeskog, who scored the go-ahead goal in Ottawa, is one of our Sleepers tonight at 22% to score. Brent Burns plays his 1,600th NHL game. Mackenzie Blackwood, our projected starter, is at +1.0 on the season. For Montreal, Juraj Slafkovský hasn't scored in ten games despite 3.3 expected goals, and Caufield has a five-game point streak.

Montreal takes 5.0 penalties a game, the kind of habit a Colorado power play creating 0.81 expected goals a night punishes, stars or not. Our playoff odds: Avalanche 95%, Canadiens 72%.
headline: Avalanche wait on MacKinnon and Makar in Montreal
